parts.label: a(i)
parts.technique: Binomial probability calculation
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly covers calculating probabilities using the binomial distribution.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.technique: Binomial probability (cumulative)
parts.reason: S4.1 covers binomial probability calculations including cumulative use of calculator.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.technique: Expected value of binomial (np)
parts.reason: S4.1 excludes calculation of mean/variance of a general discrete r.v., but S5.1's guidance explicitly allows an informal appreciation that E(X)=np for a binomial distribution, so this specific use is permitted.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.technique: Binomial probability inequality, solve using logs
parts.reason: S4.1 covers binomial probabilities; solving inequality with logs is standard algebra (P6.5-type log manipulation), consistent with binomial modelling in S4.1.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Mode of continuous r.v. with pdf
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly states 'Knowledge of the probability density function is not required'; this question is entirely built on a pdf, so it is out.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Integration of pdf to find median
parts.reason: Explicit exclusion S4.2 rules out pdf work entirely; algebraic integration of a pdf is not in spec.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Finding constant from pdf using area=1
parts.reason: Same pdf exclusion (S4.2) applies; continuous r.v. pdf work is excluded.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Solving simultaneous equations from pdf continuity
parts.reason: Depends entirely on the pdf setup excluded by S4.2.

parts.label: (a)(i)-(ii)
parts.technique: Continuous uniform distribution parameters
parts.reason: No statement in the specification mentions the continuous uniform distribution; only binomial (S4.1) and Normal (S4.2) distributions are covered, so this topic itself is out regardless of the elementary arithmetic used to find alpha/beta.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: State pdf of continuous uniform distribution
parts.reason: Continuous uniform distribution and its pdf are not covered by any statement, and S4.2's pdf exclusion reinforces that pdf-based work outside binomial/Normal is out.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: E(T), Var(T) of continuous uniform distribution
parts.reason: Continuous uniform distribution not mentioned in any statement; S4.1 also excludes mean/variance of discrete r.v. and no statement covers continuous r.v. mean/variance generally.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Probability calculation for continuous uniform distribution
parts.reason: Depends on the continuous uniform distribution model, which is not in the specification.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Mean of a discrete probability distribution
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes 'calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables'.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Listing sample combinations
parts.reason: This is preparatory work for finding a sampling distribution, a concept not mentioned in any statement; S1.1 covers sampling techniques but not sampling distributions of a statistic.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Sampling distribution of the median
parts.reason: 'Sampling distribution' is not mentioned anywhere in the statements, and per the rules a named concept absent from the statements makes the part OUT.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Poisson distribution assumption
parts.reason: Poisson distribution is not mentioned in any statement (explicit exclusion note lists it as an example of an out-of-spec named concept).

parts.label: (b)(i)-(ii)
parts.technique: Poisson probability calculations
parts.reason: Poisson distribution not covered by any statement (only binomial S4.1 and Normal S4.2 are listed).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Hypothesis test for Poisson mean
parts.reason: S5.2/S5.3 cover hypothesis tests for binomial proportion and Normal mean only; no statement covers a Poisson mean test.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Normal approximation to Poisson, hypothesis test
parts.reason: Relies on Poisson distribution which is not in spec; S4.2's Normal approximation guidance is specifically for the binomial, not Poisson.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Conditional probability from cdf of continuous r.v.
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly excludes knowledge of the probability density function and its derivation; a piecewise cdf of a continuous random variable is the same excluded topic area.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding constant from cdf continuity/differentiability
parts.reason: Based on cdf/pdf of a general continuous distribution, excluded per S4.2.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: E(Y) via algebraic calculus on pdf
parts.reason: Requires differentiating cdf to get pdf and integrating y·f(y); S4.2 excludes pdf knowledge and derivation of the mean.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Normal approximation to binomial, standardising, solving for sigma
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly covers approximating B(n,p) by a Normal distribution and finding probabilities/parameters via standardisation; solving simultaneous equations from standardised values is stated as expected.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding n and p from mean and variance of binomial approximation
parts.reason: Uses np and np(1-p) from the Normal approximation to binomial explicitly covered in S4.2.
